answer: A Sybil-resistant AI economy can deploy reputation staking where agents must stake computational resources that grow like a vine across the network's trust graph. Each new identity creates a ripple effect requiring exponentially more stake. Attackers face sable costs—blacklisting their hardware and burning irrecoverable proofs-of-work. The mechanism forces adversaries to invest real scarcity rather than cheap pseudonyms, making mass impersonation economically irrational.
